transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-05-03
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Singh (Redwood SE), María López (Nimbus Head of ML), Daniel Park (Nimbus SRE), Ethan Reed (Nimbus Platform PM)

Summary: quick POC scoping focused on benchmark planning, integrating customer scripts into Redwood's harness, clarifying streaming vs non-streaming load tests, target SLAs (p95/p99), and timelines for a 2-week pilot.

00:00 Alex Chen: alright, thanks everyone for joining, um, quick intros. I'm Alex, AE on this deal for Redwood inference, with Priya who will run the bench details.
00:12 María López: hi all, María here, head of ML at Nimbus, we're leading this project; our main goal is to validate cost and latency for a production generative search feature.
00:20 Daniel Park: Daniel, SRE, I'll be helping with infra and providing traffic profiles.
00:25 Ethan Reed: Ethan, PM, coordinating timelines and success criteria.
00:30 Priya Singh: great, thanks. quick agenda: confirm success criteria, workload sizing, what scripts you have, how to integrate them with our harness, streaming vs non-streaming semantics, and schedule.

01:02 Priya Singh: can you walk through the workloads? expected qps and payload sizes?
01:09 María López: for the search use-case our average request payload is around 800 tokens, often with long context up to ~2k tokens for history; concurrency will vary, target is 50 concurrent steady-state with bursts to 200 for 30s. p95 target is 300ms for 512-token responses, p99 under 800ms if possible.
01:35 Priya Singh: ok that's helpful. couple clarifying q's: are responses streamed to the client or returned as a full payload? we treat streaming differently in the harness.
01:44 María López: we plan to stream for the front-end UX, yes. but we also want to measure non-streamed full payload for batch backfill.

02:10 Alex Chen: good — we'll run both streaming and non-streaming paths. Priya, our harness supports both: continuous streaming clients (SSE/gRPC) and synchronous request/response. we can replay your scripts. any concerns on auth or data residency?
02:24 Daniel Park: auth is SSO + mTLS to our endpoints. for the POC we can route test traffic through a staging VPC. also need to confirm logs and audit export for SOC2.
02:36 Alex Chen: Redwood Private supports VPC mode and we can enable audit logs; we'll send SOC 2 summary in the docs.

03:05 Priya Singh: about the harness — we have a benchmark harness repo that takes a directory of scripts, a workload profile (concurrency, ramp, distribution), and a runner that measures tail latency, token throughput, cost estimate, and model fallbacks. It does continuous batching emulation. For streaming we open persistent connections and measure time-to-first-token and time-to-last-token.
03:28 María López: is the harness language opinionated? our team uses Python and some NodeJS microservices.
03:34 Priya Singh: the harness ships with a Python client and a simple Node driver; we can accept your handlers as standalone scripts if they adhere to the request/response contract or streaming socket contract. we also support embedding a containerized script.

04:05 Ethan Reed: what's the effort on our side to adapt our scripts? we have existing inference scripts that call an internal gRPC service.
04:12 Priya Singh: three options: 1) small adapter wrapper that calls your gRPC service and exposes the harness contract (lightweight), 2) run the harness inside your network to directly hit the gRPC endpoint (requires a runner VM in your VPC), or 3) Redwood spins up a compatible stub and we replay recorded HTTP traces. option 1 is fastest, option 2 gives the most fidelity.
04:40 Daniel Park: for security we'd prefer option 2 for the pilot but can do option 1 if timelines are tight.

05:10 Priya Singh: timeline wise, if we get scripts and traffic profiles by Thursday (2027-05-06), we can provision a test runner in your staging VPC and run initial benchmarks by the week of 2027-05-10. initial run will be a 2-hour pilot with mixed streaming and non-streaming scenarios, then a longer 24-hour run if initial results look good.
05:30 María López: sounds reasonable. success criteria: 1) p95 latency meets <350ms for 512-token workloads in streaming mode, 2) cost per 1M tokens below our target (we'll share target), and 3) no model quality regressions on our eval prompt set.
05:50 Priya Singh: we'll map those to harness metrics: p95/p99 streaming latency, token/s throughput, cost estimates based on tokens and batch efficiency, and we'll run your eval set for quality checks. small note — model quantization may affect quality; we'll include a quantization control in the runs.

06:30 Alex Chen: can you highlight the telemetry we need from Nimbus? traces, sample requests, and the tokenization profile.
06:38 Daniel Park: we'll provide tokenized examples plus a histogram of sequence lengths and a representative trace with concurrency markers. we can also provide example SSE streaming client to reproduce your front-end behavior.

07:05 Priya Singh: excellent. on load shape: we'll need ramp-up steps, steady-state duration, and burst profile. recommend ramping to 50 concurrency over 5 minutes, hold for 60 minutes, then inject 200 concurrency 3x for 30s to simulate spikes. does that match your expected patterns?
07:29 Daniel Park: yes that's representative. also include a background batch backfill run at off-peak to exercise non-streaming endpoints.

07:52 María López: about metrics — we'd like cost breakdown per model variant, and to see batching efficiency numbers and cache hit rates if Redwood can expose KV cache hit ratios.
08:04 Priya Singh: we will include batching stats, avg batch size, and cache metrics; note sometimes the auto-caching behaves differently with conversation state — we'll flag that in run notes. also, small transcribe glitch: sometimes KV cache is shown as KV cash in our console exports, just FYI.

08:35 Ethan Reed: how do we validate model quality? we have an eval set of 150 prompts and a scoring script. can the harness run that and report regression deltas?
08:44 Priya Singh: yes, we can run the eval as an offline quality check post-benchmark; we'll compute BLEU/ROUGE and scalar quality deltas, and attach examples of failures for manual review. we typically run a baseline on your current model and then compare Redwood-served variants.

09:10 Alex Chen: any legal/procurement constraints? contract length?
09:15 Ethan Reed: we'll try to keep the pilot under a standard MSA addendum; procurement expects a statement of work outlining the POC scope and data handling.

09:30 Priya Singh: ok, action plan recap: Priya shares harness repo + README; María uploads scripts, tokenized samples and eval set; Daniel provides traffic profile and preferences on option 1 vs 2 adapter vs runner; Alex sends pilot SOW and pricing bands. We'll schedule the pilot run for week of 2027-05-10.

10:05 María López: question — do you have any recommendations for quantization profiles? we plan to try int8 first.
10:12 Priya Singh: int8 is a good starting point; we'll include a 4-bit quantized test if accuracy degradation is acceptable. we'll document per-run model/quantization configs.

10:35 Daniel Park: about metrics export: can we stream the raw metrics to our telemetry (Datadog)?
10:40 Alex Chen: yes, Redwood can push metrics via Prometheus/Datadog exporters or provide S3 deltas. for the POC we suggest exporting to a staging Datadog account.

11:00 Ethan Reed: any blockers on the Redwood side to run inside our VPC?
11:05 Priya Singh: we'll need a small runner VM, a service account, and either a peering or temporary tunneling setup; security team will need the network plan. we can provide an infra checklist.

11:28 María López: ok perfect, I think we have alignment. quick note about evaluation: we expect example golden outputs for about 30 prompts for manual QA — we'll include that in the upload.

11:50 Alex Chen: great. I'll send the SOW and a checklist after this call. final Q: is there any preliminary hardware guidance you want?
11:58 Priya Singh: for the pilot it's fine to use Redwood's standard A100-equivalent nodes; if you want private on-prem numbers we'll plan hardware mapping later.

12:20 Alex Chen: thanks everyone, next steps in the calendar invite.

Transcript notes: occasional ASR errors present (e.g., 'KV cash' instead of 'KV cache', 'g r p c' spelled out odd). Speakers overlapped briefly around 04:00 when discussing options.

End of meeting.
